calls.title: GrowthBook Error Review
calls.summary: The meeting addressed several pressing challenges in migration and integration, particularly focusing on LaunchDarkly's options for supporting 800 Flowers' project-by-project migration preference. The team identified issues like empty string to int64 conversion errors and planned to standardize non-critical numeric fields to strings to prevent further type mismatches. Despite successful query execution, missing data in experiment results prompted deeper investigations into filtering or logic issues. The importance of collaboration was emphasized, with live screen sharing and ongoing cross-team communication facilitating faster troubleshooting. Lastly, a strategy involving UI-driven JSON unpacking was discussed to enhance query maintainability and reduce complexity within the data handling processes, with immediate follow-ups scheduled.
calls.keywords: LaunchDarkly migration, fact table query, type conversion errors, auto slice, JSON extract, managed warehouse
calls.action_items:
**Chris Sanders**
Investigate alternative migration options and script-based migration solutions for LaunchDarkly to support project-by-project approach (00:27)
Provide asynchronous migration update to 800 Flowers team before Tuesday call (01:26)
Verify and debug why no data appears in experiment results despite query execution in managed warehouse, consulting colleagues for troubleshooting support (28:43)

**Elizabeth Gilbert**
Implement changes to convert all non-critical numeric fields to string types to test impact on errors and report results (16:14)
Experiment with using UI auto unpack feature for JSON columns to improve data extraction and reduce manual SQL code changes (24:19)
Continue to verify data integrity and filtering clauses in fact table queries to isolate cause of missing data in experiment results (30:58)

**Jake Heier**
Support with documentation related to LaunchDarkly migration questions and ensure visibility on troubleshooting support discussed in channels (00:49)
